newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe threatens to sack striking doctors.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe threatens to sack striking doctors.

text.p: The Zimbabwean government ordered thousands of doctors and nurses to end their 10-day pay strike on Wednesday, threatening to sack those who defied its command and to replace them with expatriates.
The strikers, through their unions, said they would not heed the call, but were prepared to talk to the government.

"Those who do not return to work on Wednesday will be dismissed forthwith and dismissed permanently," acting Public Service, Labour and Social Welfare Minister Nathan Shamuyarira said in a statement on Tuesday night.
"They will not be allowed to reapply. The patience of government has run out," he said.
An estimated 12,000 nurses and junior doctors have been on strike since October 21, paralysing operations of the southern African state's major state hospitals.

State media say patients have died in the past week due to lack of attention at the hospitals, where senior doctors, army and Red Cross medical personnel have been handling emergencies only since the strike began.
This is the second pay strike by the doctors and nurses in two months following one in which a majority of Zimbabwe's 180,000 civil servants took part.

The strikers are demanding that President Robert Mugabe's government immediately honour its pledge made last month to consider their demands for a 60 percent wage rise, higher allowances and better working conditions.

The government says it needs more time to discuss the issue, but is facing increasing pressure as other civil servants have threatened to join the doctors and nurses on strike if talks on their demands -- similar to those of the medical workers -- are not started by November 8.
